title: Welcome!
text:
I am a second year Complex Systems Ph.D. student at the University of Vermont in Burlington. I’m a member of the Computational Story Lab at the Vermont Complex Systems Institute where I work closely with Chris Danforth and Peter Dodds.
My main, broad interest is people in complex systems.
Expected graduation date of summer 2028.

title: Welcome!
text:
Research Interests
I am interested in measuring complex, interpersonal processes in digital mediums. People are motivated to socially connect and often rely on technology and text to do so, leading me in the direction of asking how well technology facilitates this goal and how can we best measure the constructs driving this process in individual and collective levels?
Further, I like making accessible tools enabling others to conduct complexity research.

Recent News
2025

January: Our team published the py-allotax tool to pypi! We have a paper in progress describing the allotaxonometry ecosystem for researching systems. Last, I presented in Story Lab on spelunking among the natural and unnatural forms of conversation data.

2024

December: Presented in Student Complexity Research (and Pizza) seminar on additional findings regarding Heap’s law in naturalistic conversation, individual movie conversations, and entire movie scripts.
November: Presented in Story Lab on measuring emergent statistical phenomena in conversations, using Heap’s law as an information theoretic starting point–focusing on CANDOR and the Movie-Dialogs corpus.
October: worked with a team to instantiate a python interface (py-allotax) to a Story Lab tool that performs complex analysis to plot rank divergences between 2 systems.
August: Passed a qualifying exam for the program (data science methods).
July: Attended IC2S2 at University of Pennsylvania.
May-June: Biked 560 miles (10k ft elevation) of the Empire State Trail over 9 days from Buffalo, NY to NYC.
May: Finished first year of the CSDS PhD program!
May: Presented in Story Lab on linguistic coordination in the CANDOR conversation corpus.
April: Presented a poster at the UVM Student Research Conference on structuring discussion forum conversations as network data.

2023

August: Joined the Computational Story Lab and started in the PhD program in Complex Systems and Data Science.

title: About
text:
Before joining the program, I worked in various roles as a research, applied, or data scientist. I applied my prior BA and MS education in psychology to behavioral science questions, conducting work ranging from survey data collection and analysis to representing people in simulations using agent based modeling. I became more interested in how to study and evaluate systems involving people, leading me to the area of complexity science!
I am otherwise engaged in walking my dogs (River and Fen), planning my next cabin or bike trip, or having a game night.
